title: MassGoWhere: choose the visual world
question: One direction was dealt from the roll. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Colour variants of whichever you pick come next, on your phone.

options.label: The Pew Missal
options.lineage: Roman Missal two-ink printing: black text, red rubrics, silk ribbon markers
options.thesis: The answer is printed like the missal: what it is in black, what to do in red.
materials: two-ink print on thin bright paper
silk ribbon markers in liturgical colours
options.viewport: Monumental '6:30am' in black, one red rubric line 'Leave by 6:08 · 17 min by bus', the church name, and one full-width Navigate button; travel mode sits in a ribbon tab at the top edge.
options.risk: Tips into old-fashioned church printing if the type turns ornamental; it must stay a modern text face.

raised.raise: The Mass time is set monumental, the headline of every result page.
Masses you can no longer make stay visible as grey ghosts above the answer, so the pick explains itself.
Colour is reserved: the ribbon colour appears only on the one action you should take.
A thin day-line marks now, your leave-by, and the Mass, the only chart on the page.

options.label: Platform Board
options.lineage: Singapore transit wayfinding and bus-stop arrival boards
options.thesis: The next Mass arrives like the next train: minutes to go, which way, when to leave.
options.viewport: A board row 'Holy Cross · 6:30am · leave in 22 min' in countdown digits, platform-style arrow directions under it, Navigate as the exit sign.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of 'GoWhere plus transport'; feels like a transit app more than a Catholic one.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Mass times built as monumental numerals on a visible grid.
options.viewport: A giant cell-built '6:30' fills the top half; church and leave-by sit in grid cells below.
options.case: Strong on clarity (the time is unmissable); weak on audience identification, nothing about it says parish.
options.risk: Reads as a design exercise rather than a church guide.

options.label: Struck Numerals
options.thesis: Every Mass time glows faintly behind the gauze; the one you can make is struck bright.
options.viewport: Today's Mass times stacked as dim ghosts; your reachable one blazes orange with leave-by beneath.
options.case: Dramatises the mechanism perfectly; loses on audience identification and daylight legibility.
options.risk: Dark, techy mood sits oddly with a parish product and in bright sun.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One gold cord pulls a flat plane into shape.
options.viewport: A black field with one gold control.
options.case: No link to churchgoers or to finding a Mass.
options.kept: One accent, reserved for the single control.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Colour states the law each thing obeys.
options.viewport: A dusk garden with coloured rain.
options.kept: Every colour carries one meaning only.

options.label: Leather Studio
options.thesis: Digital things as loved physical objects.
options.case: Too heavy for clean and professional.
options.kept: Only the chosen item is raised; everything else lies flat.

options.label: Step Row
options.thesis: A chase light always shows where now is.
options.viewport: Sixteen keys under a running light.
options.case: Playful, off-voice for a devotional utility.
options.kept: A single line that always marks now.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A map with church pins and a bottom sheet listing the nearest Masses.
canonCard.viewport: Full-screen map, a pull-up sheet with the top three Masses and a Directions button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Google Maps, which is what users already find slow.
